subject.title: [Bug]: failed image attachment loads are silently dropped from the model prompt — model answers as if no image was sent

question: Where should OpenClaw surface failed native image attachment loads for vision-capable model turns: a model-visible prompt marker, a user/operator diagnostic, a failed turn, or a combination?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the durable behavior affects prompt text, user-facing diagnostics, path disclosure, log level, and multiple caller surfaces.

options.title: Shared Safe Prompt Marker
options.body: Return skipped-image metadata and have embedded, CLI, and harness callers add a safe model-visible count/marker without full local paths so the model cannot answer as if no image was sent.

options.title: Diagnostics Only
options.body: Emit user/operator-visible diagnostics while leaving the model prompt unchanged, which avoids prompt wording policy but still lets the model answer without the missing image.

options.title: Fail Current Turn
options.body: Treat failed current-turn native image loads as input errors, giving the strongest user signal at the cost of a stricter runtime behavior change.

recommendation.title: Shared Safe Prompt Marker
recommendation.body: Return skipped-image metadata and have embedded, CLI, and harness callers add a safe model-visible count/marker without full local paths so the model cannot answer as if no image was sent.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main blame and shared caller surfaces route most directly through Vincent Koc's recent image-loading and harness refactor work.
